name: Cardiac Hemochromatosis

criteria.description: Evidence of systemic iron overload with elevated serum ferritin and transferrin saturation
Clinical signs of cardiomyopathy including heart failure symptoms and reduced ejection fraction
Cardiac MRI showing myocardial iron deposition (T2* imaging)
Identification of HFE gene mutations or other hemochromatosis-associated mutations
Liver biopsy demonstrating iron overload (optional supportive evidence)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of systemic iron overload plus cardiac dysfunction with confirmatory cardiac MRI evidence of myocardial iron deposition
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and liver biopsy are supportive but not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic myocardial iron overload causing diastolic dysfunction

pathognomonic.symptomName: Heart failure with preserved or reduced ejection fraction

common.symptomName: Arrhythmias including atrial fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia
Hepatomegaly due to systemic iron overload

occasional.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to pancreatic iron deposition

laboratory: Elevated liver enzymes in some cases
imaging: Cardiac MRI T2* showing decreased myocardial signal consistent with iron deposition
Echocardiogram showing restrictive cardiomyopathy and reduced ejection fraction
genetic: HFE gene mutations (C282Y homozygosity or compound heterozygosity)
Other non-HFE hemochromatosis gene mutations (e.g., TFR2, HJV)
other: Liver biopsy with iron staining (Prussian blue) confirming iron overload
ECG abnormalities including arrhythmias and conduction delays

distinguishingFeatures: No myocardial iron deposition on MRI
Presence of amyloid deposits on biopsy
Characteristic imaging findings on cardiac MRI and nuclear scans

redFlags: New onset arrhythmias or conduction block
Evidence of systemic iron overload with cardiac involvement
references: Anderson LJ, et al. Cardiovascular T2* magnetic resonance for the early diagnosis of myocardial iron overload. Eur Heart J. 2001.
Barton JC, Acton RT. Hemochromatosis and iron overload: diagnosis and management. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2014.
Pennell DJ. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance in the evaluation of iron overload. Circulation. 2012.
